questions.prompt: October's invoice is 412,000 USD, but Cost Explorer's amortised cost for October is 430,000 USD. Nobody changed anything in Cost Explorer. What is the most likely explanation?
choices: Cost Explorer double counts Savings Plans and should not be trusted
Amortised cost moves the monthly share of commitment fees paid upfront in earlier months onto October's usage, while the invoice charges only what is billed in October
Taxes are left out of the invoice
The invoice is still an estimate and will be corrected
questions.explanation: Billed (cash) and effective (accrual) views are both correct and differ whenever a commitment was paid outside the period. FOCUS keeps both on every row: BilledCost for the invoice, EffectiveCost for what was consumed.

questions.prompt: A FOCUS row has ChargeCategory Purchase, a CommitmentDiscountId, BilledCost 459024.00 and EffectiveCost 0.00. What does it tell you?
choices: The provider gave the commitment away for free
The purchase was refunded later in the month
The row is invalid, because EffectiveCost must always equal BilledCost
It is a commitment purchase: its cost is carried by the EffectiveCost of the Used and Unused rows it covers, so summing EffectiveCost counts it exactly once
questions.explanation: FOCUS requires EffectiveCost to be 0 for a purchase that covers other charges and requires the covered rows to include their share. A non-zero EffectiveCost on such a row would count the commitment twice, which is why billjoin's rule checks look for it.

questions.prompt: Four database reservations show 1,008 used hours and 336 unused hours over 14 days, and every database hour in the account ran on a reservation. What are utilisation and coverage?
choices: 75% utilisation and 100% coverage: you bought more than you ran
75% utilisation and 75% coverage
25% utilisation and 100% coverage
100% utilisation and 75% coverage
questions.explanation: Utilisation is used over used plus unused in the commitment's unit: 1008 / 1344 = 75%. Coverage is the share of eligible usage that a commitment covered, and all of it was. High coverage with low utilisation is over-buying; the 336 unused hours are waste on their own Unused rows.

questions.prompt: aws ce get-cost-and-usage grouped by Type=TAG,Key=team returns a group with the key team$ and an AmortizedCost of 220.48. Which of billjoin's showback lines does it correspond to?
choices: Only (untagged)
A team whose tag value is a dollar sign
(untagged), (unused commitment) and (shared) together: every cost without a team tag, including tax, credits and the waste of untagged commitments
Only the resources whose tag value failed the tag policy
questions.explanation: Cost Explorer reports rows without the tag under key$ with an empty value. It has no separate notion of unused commitments or shared charges, so a showback copied from it pushes all of them into one unexplained remainder. Capitalised values such as team$Platform come back as their own group.

questions.prompt: Three teams each own exactly one third of 1.00 USD. Rounding each share to cents gives 0.33 + 0.33 + 0.33 = 0.99. What does billjoin do, and why?
choices: It books the missing cent to (untagged)
It leaves 0.99, because a cent is inside the invoice tolerance
It rounds every line up to 0.34 so no team is undercharged
It floors every line and gives the leftover cents to the lines with the largest remainders, 0.34, 0.33 and 0.33, so the lines add up to the total exactly
questions.explanation: The largest-remainder method keeps the rounded lines summing to the rounded total, which is what lets a chargeback journal entry balance. The invoice tolerance applies to comparing BilledCost with the invoice, not to the allocation, which must reconcile to the cent.

questions.prompt: Every instance listed by aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources has a team tag, yet the bill shows 6,000 USD of untagged EC2. What explains it, and what should you work from?
choices: The tag policy hides noncompliant resources from the Tagging API
The Tagging API only returns resources in us-east-1

GetResources returns only tagged or previously tagged resources, so instances created with no tags never appear in it; the bill still charges them, so work from the bill's untagged ResourceIds and the service's describe calls
Untagged EC2 on the bill is always the Savings Plan purchase
questions.explanation: The smoke test shows it on moto: a never-tagged instance is missing from get-resources but present in describe-instances and in the bill's untagged list. The bill is the inventory of what costs money; tags are attached to it, not the other way round.
